rounds.what: The exporter's interface was rewritten rather than patched, so the round tested the shape — whether any agent-settable value can reach any path the collector owns, by any route — rather than the three forms the fix replaced.

implementerProof.how: Round 8: I re-ran both halves of its 50-case suite rather than the passing one — 50 pass at this head, 34 fail against the script as it was at the previous head — and I enumerated the harness's agent-settable inputs myself and drove each against the new interface, which its proof does not do. Its claim that the locator is not an agent's to write I checked in the daemon's own types rather than accepting the comment that states it. Rounds 1 to 7 were each verified as those rounds record.

proof.criterion: No value an agent can set reaches any path the transcript collector owns, by any route.
proof.surface: The real `session_copy` at this head, driven with the collector's own `review-pair/reviewer.jsonl` present, after enumerating from the script which of the harness's inputs an agent can set.
proof.command: Enumerate the reads: the claim's `.sessionFile` (both callers), the claim's `.locator.sandbox.name`, `pair_agents`, the area keyword. Then drive the function with stems `../../escape`, `..`, `.`, empty, `a/b`, `x$(id)` and one holding a newline; an area of `../../etc`; and a prefix of `../../etc/`. Walk the evidence tree afterwards.
proof.observed: The agent-settable `.sessionFile` reaches only the SQL key prefix in both callers — `${pair_session%.jsonl}/` and `dirname "$launched_file"` — and names no directory at all. Every non-plain stem is refused by name with nothing written; an unknown area is refused; a prefix that looks like a traversal writes only inside the area root, because a prefix selects rows and feeds a derivation whose output is mapped to `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` and then anchored. `pair_agents` is a literal at `:1095`. Everything written landed inside the area root and the collector's own file is byte-unchanged. No route exists.
proof.negativeControl: The plain stem `podname` in the same runs copies its keys normally, so each refusal is the guard firing on that value and not the function failing; and the collector's file, placed before the runs and read after them, is what would have moved had any route existed.

proof.criterion: The suite that pins the rewritten interface is sensitive to it, not merely compatible with it.
proof.surface: `bun test scripts/e2e/lib/stage4b-session-text.test.ts`, run at this head and against the script as it was at the previous head.
proof.command: Run the suite here; then copy the e2e directory, replace `stage4b-sandbox-tree.sh` with `jj file show -r 054d4e014cf7`'s version, and run the same suite
proof.observed: 50 pass / 0 fail at this head; 16 pass / 34 fail against the previous head's script. The 34 are the half that matters: a suite passing at this head and never run against the old one would prove only that the shape compiles.
proof.negativeControl: The 16 that still pass against the old script are the control on the comparison: had the whole suite failed, the difference would have been the harness rather than the interface.

proof.criterion: The input that now names a directory is not one an agent writes.
proof.surface: The daemon's own types and write paths, read rather than inferred from the script's comment.
proof.command: Read `supervise.RequestRegister`; find every writer of a claim's locator; check the API's mentions of it
proof.observed: `RequestRegister` — the registration an agent makes — carries `Claim`, `Generation`, `Session`, `SessionFile`, `CapabilityHash` and `PluginContract`, and **no locator** (`internal/supervise/table.go:131-140`). The locator is written by the daemon from its own launch (`internal/supervise/machine.go:917`, `:1321`); the API's only other mention is a read of the stored value for a capability report (`internal/api/claims.go:180-186`). So the stem's input is the daemon's, and the plain-name refusal driven above is a second fence rather than the only one.
proof.negativeControl: `SessionFile` is in that same request type and is the value that bit twice: the asymmetry between the two fields in one struct is what makes the claim checkable rather than asserted.
